newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian gas industry official hurt in explosion.
newsitem.headline: Russian gas industry official hurt in explosion.

text.p: A senior official of huge Russian gas monopoly Gazprom was seriously injured in a bomb explosion near Moscow late on Wednesday, police said on Friday.

Vladimir Zavgorodny, a 52-year-old deputy director of Gazprom subsidiary Gazexport, was taken to a nearby hospital after a bomb exploded under his car at around 20.40 p.m. (1640 GMT), practically severing his left leg.
He was still in a coma in an unnamed hospital on Thursday, Russian newspapers reported. No information on his condition on Friday was available.
Police in Naro-Fominsk region southwest of Moscow said by telephone the motive for the attack was not known.
Medical sources said the seriousness of the injury in relation to the relatively limited damage to Zavgorodny's car appeared to suggest the attack was deliberate, and the work of professionals.

Russian businessmen are increasingly targets of violence and kidnappings in Russia's nascent market economy. A senior official from Spartak Moscow soccer club and one of her friends were shot dead last weekend.
Gazprom is the world's largest gas producer and a key exporter to eastern and western Europe. It is undergoing radical change at the hands of President Boris Yeltsin's reformist team.
Gazexport is responsible for negotiating gas contracts abroad -- a key hard-currency earner for Russia's cash-strapped economy.
